project: Prove the ACP Server with a Pinned Headless Real Client
description: Add the smallest repeatable non-editor interoperability evidence by using pinned headless acpx@0.13.0 through npx to launch the repository-built you serve acp server, initialize ACP, create a session on the default factory:@you/factory-builder target, complete one deterministic prompt/result exchange, and retain only sanitized evidence facts. Correct production behavior only if this run exposes a directly blocking defect.

context.customerAsk: Drive the repository-built you serve acp stdio server with pinned headless acpx@0.13.0 without a global acpx installation. Prove initialization, session creation with the default @you/factory-builder target, and one real prompt/result exchange using deterministic repository-supported provider effects. Retain only sanitized commands and evidence facts, do not widen into other clients or ACP lanes, and carry delivery through actual PR merge.
context.problem: The repository's own clients prove ACP framing and Factory prompting, but there is no retained evidence that an independently packaged real client can launch the built server, negotiate the protocol, observe the default Factory Builder target, cause provider execution, consume assistant output, and receive a terminal result. A manual raw transcript would not be repeatable and could leak prompts, responses, credentials, provider commands, session history, or host paths.
context.solution: Add one isolated, bounded acceptance path that builds the current you binary, invokes exactly acpx@0.13.0 through npx with a portable structured custom-agent argv for you serve acp, uses deterministic supported provider execution, asserts the required initialization/session/default-target/prompt/result/provider facts, cleans up all scenario state and processes, and emits only a redacted evidence summary. If the run reveals a reproducible blocking server defect, make only the narrow correction with focused behavioral coverage and rerun the same real-client path.

acceptanceCriteria: A documented repository command builds the current you executable and runs it as you serve acp under the real acpx@0.13.0 package via npx; it does not require or silently use a global acpx executable and does not implement another ACP client.

The real client successfully negotiates ACP and creates a session whose current target is the shipped default factory:@you/factory-builder, using a structured custom-agent argument vector that works on supported host platforms.

The same bounded run submits one ephemeral prompt, observes non-empty assistant result evidence plus a truthful terminal prompt result, and records exactly one expected deterministic provider invocation without asserting or retaining prompt or response payload text.

The run is isolated and bounded: acpx config, session, history, and cache state used by the scenario is disposable; server and provider child processes terminate; failures return a non-zero result with safe actionable classification; and deterministic observation replaces arbitrary sleeps.

Retained project documentation or test evidence identifies the repository revision, exact acpx version, sanitized command shape, initialization, session, default-target and result facts, terminal outcome, provider-invocation count, and applicable verification results while excluding prompts, raw transcript content, credentials, environment secrets, raw provider commands, and host-specific paths. Production changes occur only for a concrete defect reproduced by this run and include focused behavioral regression coverage.

Scoped quality gates pass: typecheck, documentation smoke, focused ACP and acpx tests, existing ACP functional coverage, and all required CI checks applicable to any narrow production correction. The repository-wide `make lint` baseline currently has 87 unrelated backend-size violations; that failure is retained as repository debt rather than reported as a passing ACP-lane check.

Delivery continues through implementation and review until required CI is terminal and passing, every blocking PR conversation is explicitly addressed, current-main and shared-file conflicts are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; an opened, approved, green, or ready-to-merge PR is not complete.

userStories.title: Launch the built ACP server through pinned acpx
userStories.description: As an ACP maintainer, I want a repeatable headless real-client launch path so I can verify that the independently packaged client actually initializes the repository-built stdio server and creates a session on the shipped default Factory target.
acceptanceCriteria: The acceptance path builds the current repository you executable before the run and configures acpx to launch that exact artifact with the argument vector serve, acp; it does not resolve an unrelated installed you binary.

The client is invoked as pinned acpx@0.13.0 through npx with non-interactive package installation behavior, and the evidence confirms the effective acpx version; no global acpx installation is required.
acpx uses its supported structured custom-agent argv configuration so executable paths and arguments remain unambiguous on Windows and other supported hosts.

Client configuration, session metadata and history, working state, and runtime artifacts for the scenario are isolated under disposable locations and cannot consume a developer's existing acpx sessions or credentials.
The real client completes initialize and session/new; the observable session configuration reports factory:@you/factory-builder as the current/default target.
A protocol or startup failure terminates the bounded run, returns non-zero, and reports only a safe phase/error classification without dumping JSON-RPC payloads, environment values, or local paths.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Implemented an opt-in, CI-enabled pinned acpx@0.13.0 process-boundary test that builds the current CLI, launches it with structured argv, asserts session_ensured, protocol negotiation, and the default Factory Builder target, and closes the disposable session. The run exposed a fresh-state catalog defect, corrected by initializing system packages before you serve acp. Verified with Node 22.13, focused ACP/CLI tests, docs smoke, and typecheck.

userStories.title: Complete one deterministic real-client prompt and retain safe evidence
userStories.description: As a customer evaluating ACP compatibility, I want the real headless client to complete one prompt against the default Factory Builder target so I can trust that initialization leads to actual Factory and provider execution and a terminal result, not merely a successful handshake.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting from the initialized acpx session, the acceptance path submits exactly one bounded ephemeral text prompt and observes at least one non-empty assistant result fact followed by one terminal prompt result with the truthful shipped stop reason.

The prompt uses a deterministic repository-supported provider execution path; retained provider evidence proves the expected provider identity or class, invocation count of exactly one for the bounded turn, and successful terminal outcome without retaining the prompt, generated response, raw command line, credentials, or unsafe arguments.

Assertions use acpx's machine-readable output or stable session facts rather than scraping human-formatted terminal text, while retained evidence summarizes protocol facts rather than storing a raw transcript.

The run closes input or session ownership as supported, waits on observable process completion rather than arbitrary sleeps, and leaves no you serve acp, provider, queue-owner, or scenario-owned acpx process running.

The canonical ACP documentation or test surface includes the sanitized reproduction command or template, exact acpx@0.13.0 pin, prerequisites, asserted initialization, default-target, prompt-result and provider facts, revision evidence, and cleanup behavior; placeholders replace repository roots, temporary directories, session IDs, and other host-specific values.

Runtime prompt text, assistant text, raw JSON-RPC frames, credentials, secret-bearing environment values, raw provider commands, host-specific paths, and disposable acpx history are absent from committed evidence and PR conversation artifacts.

If and only if this run reproduces a production defect that directly prevents the required exchange, the implementation corrects only that defect, adds focused behavioral coverage for the observed failure at the owning transport or service boundary, and reruns the acpx acceptance path; otherwise production ACP code remains unchanged.
Existing retention and STREAM_GAP, legal Kind and Phase projection, and broad safe-logging tests are not duplicated or expanded without a new client-observed defect in that exact behavior.
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Extended the pinned acpx@0.13.0 process-boundary proof through one ephemeral prompt, a non-empty assistant result fact, one end_turn result, and exactly one disposable Codex-shaped provider invocation. The real run exposed an ACP text-to-signature normalization defect for the shipped Factory Builder target; Factory Sessions now routes compatibility text to a signature's primary positional or stdin parameter, and Factory Builder safely derives an omitted name. Follow-up review hardens the process boundary with an allowlisted environment, process-tree cleanup on every terminal path, failure-path descendant termination coverage, a non-short required CI execution, and a sanitized terminal artifact that records the repository revision. Windows now assigns each owned client command to a kill-on-close Job Object, so descendants terminate even after a non-zero direct-parent exit; Unix retains the owned process group. The Node 22 CI lane is configured to run that proof; focused Factory Sessions coverage, packaged-factory generation/coverage, docs smoke, and typecheck remain the supporting verification. The repository-wide lint target remains blocked by 87 pre-existing backend-size findings outside this story and is explicitly retained as repository debt in the scoped quality criterion.
